standard_prerequisites.name: The class of multiplicative functions with a size condition
standard_prerequisites.statement: The functions of the class are multiplicative, and their values on square-free arguments are determined by the exponents attached to the prime factors, with a size condition on those exponents.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the class to which the dominated function belongs.

standard_prerequisites.name: Square-full and square-free decomposition
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every integer factors uniquely as a product of its square-full part and a square-free part, and this decomposition is used to split the divisors.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the first step of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Partial summation
standard_prerequisites.statement: Sums over integers of a multiplicative function can be evaluated by partial summation once the corresponding summatory function is known.
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the estimate obtained for the sum into the stated bound.

core_obligations: Split each divisor into its square-free and square-full parts and use that the square-full part of the integer is bounded by the level, so that the sum over the tuples of divisors factorises into a sum over square-free parts and a sum over square-full parts (source lines 1402-1407).
Replace the values of the function on square-free arguments by the product of the exponents attached to the prime factors, using the definition of the class (source lines 1408-1412).

Estimate the resulting sum by the standard bound for sums of a multiplicative function over square-free arguments, keeping the dependence on the level and on the two weights explicit (source lines 1413-1446).

proof_roadmap.step: Factorise the divisors into square-free and square-full parts to split the sum.
Rewrite the values of the function on square-free arguments through the exponents.
Apply the summatory estimate and partial summation to reach the stated bound.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled lemma at source lines 1394-1399: for x beyond a universal threshold and for a level between two and the fourth power of the logarithm, the smooth part of the convolution sum is bounded by a constant times the logarithm of the level over the square root of the level, times an explicit factor in which the two weights appear. The author gave it no label, so its position in the article is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 1401-1446) proceeds by splitting every divisor into its square-free and square-full parts, which turns the sum into a product of a sum over square-free parts and a sum over square-full parts; the values of the function on square-free arguments are then rewritten through the exponents attached to the prime factors, and the resulting sum is estimated with a standard summatory bound and partial summation, which is where the explicit dependence on the level and on the two weights is produced. The statement records only the final shape of the bound.
